Pipeline parallelism + MLA: making it actually work

I've been running Kimi K2 and GLM-4.6 through vLLM with LMCache for a while now, and kept hitting the same wall: the moment you turn on pipeline parallelism with more than one LMCache server, the connector flat-out refuses to start. The error message says "only supports tensor parallelism (TP), not pipeline parallelism (PP)" — which is fair enough as a guard, but it meant I was stuck choosing between PP (which my hardware layout needs) and LMCache (which my workload needs).

So I dug into why the guard was there, and it turned out to be a really subtle locking bug that's fixable without redesigning the protocol. Here's what I found and what I changed.

The actual problem

compute_extra_count decides how many read locks to acquire on each KV chunk in L1. For MLA models, all TP workers within a rank-shard share the same KV object, so you need tp_size - 1 extra locks (one per additional reader). The old code inferred whether a model was MLA by checking tp > world_size — if the tensor-parallel size was bigger than the world size, it assumed MLA (because vLLM divides world_size by tp for MLA).

That heuristic works fine when PP=1. But the moment PP > 1, world_size = tp × pp, so the heuristic collapses. Concretely: TP=4, PP=2, 2 servers gives you wire tp_size=2 and world_size=2, so 2 > 2 is false → extra_count = 0 → the server locks 1 copy but 4 workers try to read it → premature eviction → silent KV corruption. The guard was there to stop you from hitting that.

What I changed

Rather than inferring MLA, I made it explicit. IPCCacheServerKey now carries a use_mla flag — same backward-compatible msgspec field pattern as the existing cache_salt (old payloads without it decode as False, which is safe). The adapters set it from ParallelStrategy.use_mla, which already gets it from vLLM's model_config.use_mla.

With the flag explicit, compute_extra_count becomes trivially correct: tp_size - 1 if use_mla else 0. No guessing.

But while testing that, I found two more issues in ParallelStrategy that the PP guard was also papering over:

kv_tp_size was tp_size // n_servers, which assumes TP groups split evenly across servers. They don't — the connector assigns servers by contiguous rank blocks (server_urls[rank // ranks_per_node]), so under PP the server blocks align with pipeline stages and all tp_size TP ranks of a stage land on one server. The correct formula is min(tp_size, ranks_per_node).

is_kv_writer had the same blind spot. It used rank % (tp_size // n_servers), which picked multiple writers per shard under PP (double-stores) and zero writers on some servers when PP=1 and ns>1 (missing stores). The fix is (rank % ranks_per_node) % tp_size == 0, which gives exactly one writer per (server, pipeline-stage) pair.

I also cleaned up the other adapters while I was at it — the TensorRT-LLM adapter had tp_size hardcoded to 1 in its LOOKUP calls, and the SDK was sending world_size where it should have sent the reader count. Both now take the value as a parameter.

A tip for anyone debugging this kind of thing

The thing that took me the longest was realizing that the comment above the PP guard said "Non-MLA mode is not affected by this restriction" — but the actual code checked if n_servers > 1 with no MLA gate at all. The code was stricter than the comment. If you're ever staring at a guard that seems overly conservative, check whether the comment matches the condition. Sometimes the guard was written for a bug that's since been fixed elsewhere, and nobody went back to relax it.

Testing

I wrote a standalone test runner (run_pp_fix_tests.py) that works without torch/vllm installed — it stubs the heavy intermediate modules and tests the actual edited source. 60 checks covering:

  • compute_extra_count for 9 TP×PP×ns×MLA combos
  • IPCCacheServerKey.use_mla round-trip, identity, and msgpack wire backward-compat
  • lookup() / free_lookup_locks() integration (extra_count flows correctly)
  • kv_tp_size + is_kv_writer lock-balance for 12 MLA combos (one writer per (server, stage), acquire = release)
  • Source-inspection checks that every adapter sets use_mla on keys

There's also a pytest version (test_pipeline_parallel_fix.py) for running in a full env.

What I couldn't do here

I'm on Apple Silicon so I couldn't run an actual CUDA inference test. The lock-balance math is exhaustively verified, but a real multi-GPU PP run would be the final confirmation. If anyone with an H100 or A100 rig wants to try --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 4 with Kimi K2 + 2 LMCache servers, that'd be the definitive test.

Compatibility

  • Wire-compatible with old servers/clients (msgspec field-default)
  • model_config.use_mla is already set correctly for Kimi K2 (kimi_linear) and GLM-4.5/4.6 (glm4_moe_lite) in vLLM's is_deepseek_mla() — I verified this against vLLM main
  • DP guard is retained (that's a separate limitation, not touched here)

Code Review

This pull request enables pipeline parallelism (PP) support in multi-server MLA deployments by introducing an explicit use_mla flag in IPCCacheServerKey and propagating it through the SGLang, TRT-LLM, vLLM, and SDK adapters. This replaces a fragile heuristic in compute_extra_count that previously caused under-locking and premature KV eviction under PP. The review feedback correctly identifies a fragile test (test_multi_server_dp_still_blocked) that uses source-code string inspection to verify the DP guard, which violates the repository style guide rule that tests should verify public interfaces rather than implementation details.

Thanks for the review @gemini-code-assist — good catch on the source-string-inspection test. That was a shortcut I took to avoid pulling in vLLM as a test dependency, but you're right that it violates the repo style guide and would break on any rename.

Fixed in b6ed1c5:

  1. Extracted _validate_multi_server_config into a standalone module (lmcache/integration/vllm/multi_server_config.py) that has zero vLLM/ZMQ imports. This means it can be unit-tested directly without mocking the connector's heavy dependencies.

  2. Replaced the source-inspection test with three behavioral tests that call _validate_multi_server_config directly:

    • test_multi_server_dp_still_blocked — passes a config with dp_size=2, n_servers=2 and asserts ValueError with "data parallelism"
    • test_multi_server_config_world_size_divisibility — passes a non-divisible world_size and asserts AssertionError
    • test_multi_server_config_valid — passes a valid PP+MLA config and asserts no exception

The connector still re-exports _validate_multi_server_config for backward compatibility, but the canonical implementation lives in the lightweight module.

Also took the opportunity to add explicit ROCm detection (is_rocm property on CudaDeviceSpec via torch.version.hip). ROCm already works through PyTorch's CUDA compat layer — this just makes the detection explicit for logging and metrics.

Fair ask. Honest answer: we haven't run this against a real multi-server pipeline-parallel setup yet — reproducing the actual PP+MLA scenario (>1 LMCache server, an MLA model like Kimi K2/GLM-4.6) needs enough GPUs/machines to genuinely exercise the distributed path, and we don't have much hardware to test that at scale right now.

What we have verified: the unit tests added in b6ed1c5 (test_multi_server_dp_still_blocked, test_multi_server_config_world_size_divisibility, test_multi_server_config_valid) cover the locking/config logic directly, and those pass. But that's not the same as a real end-to-end run under load, and we won't claim it is.

We're working on getting access to a proper multi-server test rig so we can post real logs/screenshots from an actual PP+MLA run rather than asserting it works. Will follow up here once we have that.

Support pipeline parallelism with MLA models in multi-server MP mode
df6bde9 
The multi-server MP connector raised ValueError for any deployment with
pp_size > 1. The root cause was in compute_extra_count, which inferred
MLA from a tp > world_size heuristic — under PP that heuristic misfires
(PP inflates world_size) and produces extra_count = 0, causing
under-locking and premature KV eviction.

This replaces the heuristic with an explicit use_mla flag carried in
IPCCacheServerKey (backward-compatible msgspec field, same pattern as
cache_salt), fixes kv_tp_size and is_kv_writer to account for
PP-aligned contiguous server blocks, and propagates use_mla across all
client adapters (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, SDK).

Fix P0 bugs: registry collision + NameError, plus NITs
09387b9 
P0 fixes:
- platform/__init__.py: changed _DEVICE_REGISTRY from dict to list.
  The dict comprehension was last-wins, so RocmDeviceSpec (device_type=

- rocm/ipc_wrapper.py: removed unused torch_device_type import

Fix double-free, SGLang MLA object keys, ROCm pin_memory fallback
19b3d80 
Critical:
- abort-leak fix: now frees only unretrieved tail [num_vllm_hit,
  num_lmcache_hit) instead of [0, num_lmcache). Prevents double-free
  warnings on normal completion (the range [0, num_vllm_hit) was
  already freed by update_state_after_alloc + per-worker RETRIEVE).
- test_pp3_aligned_configs_pass: moved 5 configs that are rejected
  by the validator (rpn%tp!=0) to test_pp3_misaligned_configs_rejected.
  The test would have failed at runtime because the validator is
  stricter than the lock-balance math (rejects writer-misaligned
  configs even when locks would balance via min(tp,rpn) clamping).
- SGLang adapter: world_size and worker_id now correct for MLA
  (world_size=1, worker_id=0 instead of tp_size and rank). Without
  this fix, SGLang MLA deployments would produce incorrect object
  keys leading to cache misses.

Platform:
- rocm/pin_memory.py + rocm/ipc_wrapper.py: fixed duplicate
  find_library('amdhip64') bug — both iterations used the same
  lib_name, so fallback paths were unreachable when find_library
  returned a non-loadable path. Now tries find_library result first,
  then hardcoded fallbacks.

Tests:
- non-MLA COMBOS test: removed tautology (was tp//ns == tp//ns and
  0==0, always true). Now tests the actual invariant (extra=0,
  locked=1, 1 reader per shard).
- Removed dead 'Force re-import' code in registry test (was a no-op
  loop with pass body).
- Updated abort-leak test to verify start=num_vllm_hit_tokens.

138/138 tests pass.

  (when neither is_available). Prevents RocmPinMemoryBackend from

  single-server only).

Support EP, TP, PP, DP, DCP on any servers, any NVIDIA/AMD hardware
372adc4 
EP: already fully supported (shards MoE experts, not KV cache).

Fix 1: ObjectKey bitmap overflow (CRITICAL)
- Widened from 8-bit to 16-bit fields (64-bit int)
- Supports up to 65535 GPUs per field (was 255 → silent corruption)
- Added validation asserts

Fix 2: Data Parallel (DP) support
- Added dp_rank/dp_size fields to IPCCacheServerKey (backward-compat)
- ParallelStrategy computes dp_server_offset for server URL routing
- build_parallel_strategy reads data_parallel_size from vLLM config
- multi_server_config: DP no longer hard-rejected; validates
  n_servers % dp_size == 0
- Connector applies dp_offset to server URL index

Fix 3: DCP/PCP awareness
- Added dcp_size/pcp_size fields to ParallelStrategy
- kv_tp_size: min(tp * dcp_size, rpn) for MLA (DCP workers share KV)
- build_parallel_strategy reads decode_context_parallel_size
- is_kv_writer uses effective_tp accounting for DCP

Fix 4: Relaxed MLA alignment for large server counts
- When rpn < tp_size, min(tp, rpn) clamping makes lock-balance work
- Validator now allows rpn < tp (e.g. 16 servers, TP=8, PP=4)
- Only rejects when rpn >= tp and rpn % tp != 0

Fix 5: Mixed-vendor safety
- Added device_vendor field to IPCCacheServerKey
- _create_key sets 'nvidia' or 'rocm' via _is_rocm()/_has_cuda()
- Prevents cross-vendor key aliasing in mixed clusters

Fix 6: Async fan-out for many servers
- LOOKUP uses ThreadPoolExecutor when n_servers > 4
- Prevents single slow server from blocking entire fan-out

Fix 7: Duplicate server URL validation
- Connector checks for duplicate URLs in server_urls config

Fix 8: Stale comment (local_world_size: 8 → 65535)
